title.quote: LLMs and Stack Overflow Discussions: Reliability, Impact, and Challenges
title.justification: This is the title printed at the beginning of the paper.
title.value: LLMs and Stack Overflow Discussions: Reliability, Impact, and Challenges

extractions.description: An empirical software-engineering study that mines Stack Overflow activity, prompts ChatGPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2-7b on sampled questions, and evaluates generated answers with embedding similarity, semantic judgments, sentiment analysis, manual categorization, and statistical tests.

type.quote: We conducted an empirical study analyzing questions from Stack Overflow and using these LLMs to address them.
type.justification: The work collects data, executes models, and performs quantitative and manual analyses.

name.quote: evaluating the reliability of LLMs in Software Engineering while assisting developers with their daily tasks is a relevant and important topic
name.justification: The paper evaluates LLM-generated answers in a software-engineering setting.

name.quote: Previous studies also investigate the impact of ChatGPT on posting activities on Q&A communities.
name.justification: The paper advances study of developer Q&A communities by measuring Stack Overflow activity and user behavior.

name.quote: With the advance of Large Language Models (LLMs), practitioners and researchers have explored the potential of leveraging LLMs for different software engineering tasks
name.justification: LLM evaluation is central to the paper, though the application and claimed contribution are specifically tied to software-engineering questions.

name.quote: we mined SO posts and collected the data using SO’s API
name.justification: Mining and analyzing repository/forum data is a central empirical setting of the study.

name.quote: For that, we perform a sentiment analysis of the generated answers.
name.justification: NLP methods including embeddings and sentiment analysis are used to evaluate answer text.

name.quote: we focus on ChatGPT-3.5
name.justification: This is the principal OpenAI model evaluated in the study.

is_executed.justification: The authors queried this model through its API.
